title: FACT: Fixed-Budget Allocation and Cross-Step Training for Speculative Decoding
abstract: arXiv:2611.23463v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates language-model generation by verifying multiple draft tokens in a single target-model pass. However, better draft predictions and longer accepted continuations do not necessarily produce faster generation. To examine this gap, we present FACT (Fixed-Budget Allocation and Cross-Step Training), an experimental framework for studying how drafter training, candidate allocation, and execution conditions jointly affect acceptance and latency. Using a lightweight feature-prediction drafter with a frozen Llama-3-8B-Instruct target under greedy decoding, we first examine how training translates into accepted tokens. Backpropagating through predicted-feature rollouts with greater weight on early steps improves acceptance by 15-24% over uniformly weighted detached training, yet average rollout proxy cross-entropy does not reliably rank drafters by acceptance. translated_title: FACT：面向推测解码的固定预算分配与跨步训练
translated_abstract: 推测解码通过在单次目标模型前向传播中验证多个草稿token来加速语言模型生成。然而，更好的草稿预测和更长的被接受续写并不一定能带来更快的生成速度。为探究这一差距，我们提出了FACT（固定预算分配与跨步训练），这是一个用于研究草稿模型训练、候选token分配与执行条件如何共同影响接受率和延迟的实验框架。在贪婪解码设置下，我们使用轻量级的特征预测草稿模型配合冻结的Llama-3-8B-Instruct目标模型，首先考察了训练如何转化为被接受的token。通过对预测特征rollout进行反向传播，并对早期步骤赋予更大权重，相比均匀加权的分离训练可将接受率提升15-24%；然而，平均rollout代理交叉熵并不能可靠地按接受率对草稿模型进行排序。除预测质量之外，草稿候选的放置位置……
tldr: 提出FACT实验框架，系统研究草稿模型训练、候选token分配与执行条件对推测解码接受率和延迟的联合影响，并提出对早期步骤加重权重的跨步训练方法，使接受率相比传统分离训练提升15-24%。
en_tdlr: FACT is an experimental framework that studies how drafter training, candidate allocation, and execution conditions jointly affect acceptance and latency in speculative decoding, introducing cross-step training with greater weight on early steps that improves acceptance by 15-24% over uniformly weighted detached training.
